result.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision
result.summary: The Safety-Aware Denoiser (SAD) is a recent, training-free, safety-guidance framework for text diffusion models. During inference, SAD steers text samples toward safe regions of the token probability space. In this paper, we propose $\mathit{SADDER}$ (Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision), which improves the safety and quality trade-offs of SAD by exploiting a safety-guidance signal in the embedding (or activation) space for each token position, then updating the token positions using the SAD update rule multiplied by the guidance signal. This multiplication acts as a gating mechanism: tokens with a high unsafe signal are more likely to be modified during inference following the SAD update rule. However, such an update does not automatically preserve the conditional mean, i.e., the denoiser of a fixed target distribution. We therefore theoretically derive new position-wise target distributions for which the modified denoiser is exact. Furthermore, we derive conditions under which the position-wise target distributions match a global target distribution. We test our $\mathit{SADDER}$ method on popular Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) and Uniform-State Diffusion Models (USDMs) across unsafe continuation and jailbreak settings, and show that $\mathit{SADDER}$ achieves a better balance between safety, generation quality, and inference cost than existing methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SADDER：在文本扩散模型推理时，按 token 位置从嵌入（激活）空间提取安全引导信号，并用该信号对 SAD 式更新规则加权修正 token，同时从理论上推导出使修改后去噪器保持精确的逐位置目标分布，并在 MDLM/USDM 的不安全续写与越狱设置上验证安全性与质量的权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「嵌入空间逐位置引导信号 + 门控式状态更新 + 目标分布校正以保持去噪一致」可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的定向修改、视觉证据筛选门控与更新后的一致性约束提供可供核查的方法线索；但该工作面向文本扩散安全引导，与视觉/多模态推理无直接联系。
